data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise advanced prepositional phrases and idiomatic combinations used in formal and everyday B2 English.
learningPoints: Distinguish idiomatic combinations that cannot be translated word for word.
Use formal phrases such as in accordance with and in response to.
Use common expressions such as on purpose, by chance and under pressure.
Choose the correct preposition according to the whole phrase.
Build fluency by learning complete multi-word units.

sections.explain: IN CHARGE OF means responsible for something or someone.

words.word: She is in charge of the marketing team.
She is on charge of the marketing team.
She is in charge for the marketing team.
He broke the rule on purpose.
He broke the rule by purpose.
He broke the rule in purpose.

sections.explain: BY CHANCE means accidentally or unexpectedly.

words.word: I met her by chance at the station.
I met her on chance at the station.
I met her in chance at the station.

sections.explain: UNDER PRESSURE is a fixed phrase meaning experiencing stress or demands.

words.word: People often make mistakes when they are under pressure.
People often make mistakes when they are in pressure.
People often make mistakes when they are on pressure.

sections.explain: IN RESPONSE TO introduces what caused a reaction or reply.

words.word: The company changed its policy in response to customer complaints.
The company changed its policy on response to customer complaints.
The company changed its policy in response for customer complaints.

sections.explain: IN ACCORDANCE WITH means following a rule, agreement or standard.

words.word: The work was completed in accordance with the regulations.
The work was completed according with the regulations.
The work was completed in accordance to the regulations.

sections.explain: AT RISK OF means in danger of experiencing something.

words.word: The building is at risk of flooding.
The building is in risk of flooding.
The building is at risk for flood.

sections.explain: IN FAVOUR OF means supporting an idea or proposal.

words.word: Most members voted in favour of the proposal.
Most members voted on favour of the proposal.
Most members voted in favour for the proposal.

sections.explain: ON BEHALF OF means representing another person or group.

words.word: She accepted the award on behalf of the team.
She accepted the award in behalf of the team.
She accepted the award on behalf for the team.

sections.explain: WITH REGARD TO is a formal phrase meaning concerning or about.

words.word: With regard to your application, we need more information.
With regards of your application, we need more information.
With regard for your application, we need more information.
